decisions.evidence: Maker round 2: “Saving should capture useful page details automatically; tags and search should make links easy to retrieve; ‘read later’ should keep a focused reading pile; and archiving should tidy finished items away without deleting them.” Client round 2: “Yes, that's exactly it.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level goal decisions during goal confirmation.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4: “saving requires only the web address.” Client round 4: “I pasted only the address and it pulled in a clear title…”
decisions.note: The prototype save flow conforms to saving a bookmark by URL.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 6–8: “click Add label, type the label, and press Enter; the label stays visible on the bookmark card.” Client round 8: “adding a visible label right on the card… looks right.”
decisions.note: The settled inline-label flow assigns tags and exposes them on the bookmark card.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 9: “search covers titles, descriptions, originating sites, and labels from one box.” Client round 9 approves matches through a label and description but does not mention the omitted bookmark note or full URL fields.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the explicitly enumerated search corpus omits notes and does not establish full-URL search.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 9 instructs the client to type plain `learning`, which matches a label. Client round 9 explicitly accepts the difference: “I typed one word… and it found the link through its label… That's how I'd expect search to work.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: plain text implicitly searches tags instead of requiring `#tag`; the client explicitly states and accepts that behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 11–13: the Read later control marks a bookmark and a separate sidebar view shows the focused pile while the item remains in the full collection. Client round 13: “just what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The settled reading-pile behavior conforms to marking and separately viewing unread bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 14–16: “Archived bookmarks leave the active collection but retain their page details and labels in the Archive view.” Client round 16 confirms this behavior.
decisions.note: The archive interaction conforms to hiding archived items from the active collection and showing them separately.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 18: “an incomplete address should never create a bookmark until it is corrected.” Client round 18 agrees it should “hold off on creating a bookmark until there's a real address.”
decisions.note: The URL-required validation edge case conforms to the bookmark URL constraint.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 19: entering `Learning` when `learning` exists leaves the existing label unchanged and reports it already present. Client round 19 approves avoiding the duplicate.
decisions.note: The duplicate-label decision conforms to tag-name uniqueness; case folding is an orthogonal implementation choice.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 21 presents an empty but dedicated Read later view. Client round 21 says it is better than redirecting to all bookmarks.
decisions.note: The empty-state decision preserves the separate unread perspective.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 22 presents an empty Archive that remains open. Client round 22 approves the dedicated empty archive view.
decisions.note: The empty-state decision preserves the separate archived-bookmark perspective.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 23: archiving a reading-pile item removes it from Read later and All bookmarks and preserves it in Archive. Client round 23: “That's the right result.”
decisions.note: The interaction conforms to archived items being excluded from active perspectives and retained in the archive.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 24 proposes “keeping the single existing bookmark and explaining that another copy was not added.” Client round 24 approves duplicate prevention but never asks to be guided into editing the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the flow prevents a duplicate but omits the required edit-existing guidance; the missing guidance is not surfaced.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 25: removing the Read later mark makes the item disappear from that pile while retaining it in All bookmarks. Client round 25 describes this as “Marking something as read.”
decisions.note: The toggle conforms to marking a bookmark read and removing it from the unread view.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 27–29: Edit details changes a saved title or description and displays the result on the card. Client round 29 confirms being able to edit the title or description after saving.
decisions.note: This recorded portion of the edit flow conforms for post-save title and description editing; completeness of editable fields is classified separately at the scope gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 30: Restore returns an archived bookmark to All bookmarks with its details and labels intact. Client round 30 says this confirms “archiving never really lost anything.”
decisions.note: The restore flow makes archiving reversible and returns the item from the separate archive.

decisions.evidence: Across maker rounds 4 and 17, the checked collected details are described around title and description; maker round 31 closes implementation scope as the 17 checked flows. Client round 31 says the limited scope “covers everything” without identifying missing favicon and preview-image collection.
decisions.note: Specification gate, carried unchanged into round 32 implementation review: automatic metadata collection is incomplete relative to the required title, description, favicon, and preview image set.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 27–29 only present editing an already-saved bookmark; maker round 31 proposes implementing the settled scope. Client round 31 approves without requesting title/description editing before save.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the scope includes post-save editing but omits pre-save editing of collected metadata.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 29 defines Edit details as changing “the saved title and description,” while labels use their separate flow; maker round 31 closes this as implementation scope. Client approval does not request URL or note editing.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the settled editing scope omits editing the bookmark URL and note.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 enumerates the complete implementation scope, including reversible archiving but no delete flow. Client round 31: “that scope covers everything I set out to do.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: permanent bookmark deletion is absent from the proposed scope and the client does not surface it.

decisions.evidence: Maker presentations describe cards exposing titles, descriptions, sites, and labels, and round 31 closes those checked flows as scope; no favicon is included. Client round 31 approves the scope without mentioning it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the list-card specification omits the required favicon exposure.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 presents all 17 settled flows as the implementation scope, but none defines selecting a bookmark item to navigate to its original URL. Client round 31 approves the scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate: original-URL navigation from a list item is missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 6–8 settle tag entry as “click Add label, type the label, and press Enter”; round 31 closes that flow as scope. Client approvals never request suggestions from existing tags.
decisions.note: Specification gate: existing-tag autocomplete is omitted from the tag-entry behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 enumerates inline labels and unified search within the complete scope, but no behavior selects a displayed tag to filter the collection. Client round 31 approves without requesting it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: direct filtering by selecting a specific tag is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 9–10 define the unified search fields, and round 31 includes that checked search in implementation scope, but no case-insensitive matching rule is specified. Client round 31 approves without raising it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: case-insensitive search is missing from the settled search contract.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 closes the demonstrated one-word unified search as the implementation scope; no AND/OR/NOT operators, parentheses, or literal-operator quoting rule were presented. Client round 31 approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate: boolean and grouped search syntax is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 closes the demonstrated search behavior as scope without any exact quoted-phrase search. Client round 31 approves the scope without requesting it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: exact quoted-phrase search is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 states that the 17 individual-item flows are the implementation scope; no multi-selection or bulk action is included. Client round 31 approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate: selecting multiple bookmarks for bulk tag, state, archive, or delete actions is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 proposes the complete scope without an action over the entire currently filtered collection. Client round 31 says the scope covers everything.
decisions.note: Specification gate: filter-scoped whole-collection bulk actions are absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 enumerates the settled collection functionality but includes no sort control or sort key. Client round 31 approves the scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bookmark-list sorting is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 closes implementation scope around page details, labels, search, reading, and archive; no bookmark note or rendered markdown is included. Client round 31 approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate: markdown notes and rendered note viewing are absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 presents the complete implementation scope without local page snapshots or PDF preservation. Client round 31 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: local single-file HTML snapshots and the PDF-download rule are absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 presents the complete scope without Internet Archive snapshot creation. Client round 31 approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Internet Archive snapshot support is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 14–16 and 30 establish reversible archive/restore, while round 31 closes a scope containing no permanent delete operation. Client round 31 approves without requesting the delete side of the distinction.
decisions.note: Specification gate: archive is reversible, but the required archive-versus-permanent-delete distinction is incomplete because deletion is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 presents the full scope with unified search and labels but no saved combination of search terms and included/excluded tags. Client round 31 approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate: reusable saved-filter bundles are absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 presents the implementation scope without bookmark import. Client round 31 approves it as complete.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Netscape HTML import preserving title, tags, and date is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 presents the implementation scope without bookmark export. Client round 31 approves it as complete.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Netscape HTML export is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 31 presents the complete scope without personal display settings; round 32 says the production app implements the approved flows. Client rounds 31–32 accept without requesting default-sort, displayed-item, or font-size settings.
decisions.note: Specification gate, carried unchanged into implementation review: display-related personal settings are absent.
